title: EDGE: ZPK.TransferFunction merges distinct poles within 100*eps window, wrong numerators
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #70 fuzz/AULHZC] ZPK.TransferFunction gives wrong numerators when distinct poles fall in its merge window. commonDenomPoles and poleSetDifference (zpk.go:369,399) treat poles within 100*eps*(1+|p|) as equal, so a real pole can match a complex one. sortConjugatePairs (zpk.go:322) then re-adds the conjugate and the numerator degree is too high (polynomial_channel.go:90). Repro 1: NewZPKMIMO(zeros {{nil,nil}}, poles {{{1e-14+1e-14i, 1e-14-1e-14i},{1e-15}}}, gains {{1,1}}, dt 0) -> TransferFunction gives Den=[1 -2e-14 2e-28] and Num[0][1] equal to Den, so tf.Eval(10)[0][1] = 1 but zpk.Eval = 0.1. Repro 2 (unit scale): poles {1+-1e-15i} and {1} -> Den=[1 -2 1], Num1=[1 -2 1], tf(3)[1] = 1 vs zpk(3) = 0.5. MATLAB tf(zpk) converts each channel separately and gets this right. FuzzZPKToTF skips these rows with reason 'distinct row poles within the ZPK pole-merge tolerance'.

title: EDGE: DCGain wrong finite value / wrong Inf next to near-DC or exact DC poles
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The A solve fails (cond 1.4e21) and poleSpacing near=true (pole -1.88e-8). DCGain returns +9.684e11. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Example dc9: a continuous upper-triangular A with diagonal entries -2.89e-5, -3.09e-11, -1.75e-5, ... gives DCGain [-Inf, -78626.6], while FreqResponse(0) and the exact big.Rat solve give [-1.1129e18, -3.0967e18]. Another: discrete 2x2 A=[0.9998853776327908 0.0001224178710512369; -6.299779160740249e-05 1.000067282291557], B=[-0.7525840543357618 -1.8936563902987011; -0.3336326973535324 -0.8822404525470022], C=[-1.3323341784633906 -0.2326700817740477; 0.48991627788123343 0.8587983672300241], dt=0.01. Its DCGain is finite but has relative error 5e-5 against the exact value (789372732529716 vs 789410222466333), and FreqResponse(0) is +Inf in every entry. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). DCGain[1,0] = 6.73e13; exact rational limit on the float model is +Inf (det(I-A) = 0 exactly, exact pole order 1, computed eigenvalue 2e-15 from 1). The value comes from dcGainByStructuralEntries. dcGainByBlockLaurent declines because it needs a 1x1 block with A_kk == x0, although the branch's exactDetIsZero could detect this block. Files: response.go dcGainByStructuralEntries / dcGainByBlockLaurent.

Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1,A=[-1000 10; 0 0], b=[1;1], c=[1 1], d=0). Exact residue at s=0 is 1.01, so the DC gain is infinite (MATLAB dcgain gives Inf). title: Fuzz: discretization c2d/d2c all methods
body:
Targets: Discretize (ZOH, FOH, Tustin with/without prewarp, matched, impulse, least squares, Thiran/fractional delay), D2C, D2D.
Oracle: independent expm (scaling-squaring in big.Float or high-order Padé) for ZOH/FOH; bilinear map by direct evaluation for Tustin; d2c(c2d(G)) ≈ G where defined; frequency response match to method's analytic formula; stability preservation (stable in → stable out for ZOH/Tustin).
Skip: methods documented unsupported for the regime (e.g. D2C with poles at z≤0).

title: CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF/Reduce count rounding-noise SVs as rank (per-block relative threshold)
body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Common root: staircase.go threshold := tol*fnorm per block, absFloor only on block norm. Fix: per-SV threshold max(tol*||block||, absFloor) / MATLAB absolute default. Cross-ref PKUP2G and JBKTCQ (opposite direction: absolute floor drops tiny B) - fix must reconcile both.

[w12f #26 fuzzstruct/GHNJYJ] CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF/Reduce (staircase.go:114 `threshold := tol * fnorm`) count rounding noise as rank whenever a staircase block is small compared with ‖A‖. absFloor is applied only to the whole block's norm, not to each singular value. Primary repro, reproduces on both arm64 and amd64: A=[-1e4 0 0 0; 0 -1 0 0; 1 0 -2 0; 0 1e-13 0 -3], B=[1 0; 0 1; 0 0; 0 0], C=[1 1 1 1]. CtrbF(A,B,C,0).K=[2 2] and Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable).Order=4. With A[3,1]=0 K=[2 1]. The 1e-13 coupling is 1e-17 relative to ‖A‖, which MATLAB's absolute default tol (10·n·norm(A,1)·eps ≈ 9e-11) would treat as zero. Secondary repro, arm64 only (passes on amd64): s:=fzDecode(t,0xba,[0 1.5 66 1.5 0.7 25 0 0 0 -10 0.37 0 0.5 0 68.7 0.3]); e:=fzExtend(s). ObsvF gives K=[2 2 2] (6 states) although the exact rational rank is 5 (two exactly unobservable states injected). Step trace: singular values [5.78, 3.99e-13], threshold tol·fnorm=6.29e-14, absFloor=1.03e-9, so 3.99e-13 is counted. Suggested fix: per-singular-value threshold max(tol·‖block‖, absFloor). Reduce ReduceAll/ReduceUnobservable go wrong the same way (e.g. fuzz tuple kind=0xa8: 7 states kept, 5 expected). Not to be confused with the precision limit on ill-conditioned staircases (noise 5e-10 above the floor), which is not this bug.

[w12f #38 fuzzstruct/review0] CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF and Reduce (minreal) keep structurally unobservable/uncontrollable states. Cause: staircase.go uses a relative rank threshold for each block (tol*||block||_F, tol=n^2*eps), so in a small later block a singular value at rounding-noise level (~1e-14) clears the threshold (~3.7e-15). MATLAB ctrbf/obsvf use a default tolerance that is absolute in ||A|| (10*n*norm(A,1)*eps per the docs; I recalled this, did not run MATLAB), which would reject that noise. Repro: FuzzCtrbF input kind=0xda vals=[-1 335 58.25 3 -89.8125 0.13333333333333333 -40 0 -45 -4.3125 -78.92222222222222 0.6 -2 0 -6.6000000000000005 0.3] through fzExtend gives N=10: a 6-state core (poles -0.003, ±0.1i, -1000±9950i, ||A||_F=2.4e4, C~1e6) plus 2 states with exactly zero B rows that the core never drives and 2 states with exactly zero C columns that never drive the core. Results: ObsvF K=[3 3 3] (9 observable), but its own Abar/Cbar show state 1 with Cbar column <=2e-21 and Abar coupling <=6e-13, which is unobservable by the library's own absolute floor (5.4e-10). A reference SVD staircase with an absolute floor finds 8, with a 1e3 gap on each side of every rank decision. Downstream: Sminreal returns 6 states (correct), Reduce(ReduceUnobservable) returns 9 (expected <=8), Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable) and Reduce(ReduceAll) return 10, and CtrbF gives K=[2 2 2 2 2]. Same result on amd64. Files: staircase.go:66-125 (absFloor and threshold := tol*fnorm), ctrbobsv.go:105-141 (doc says the tolerance deliberately differs from MATLAB). The I/O response is unaffected; only the order/minimality is wrong. Coordinator: the author may already have filed a variant; please dedupe.

[w12f #41 fuzzstruct/review1] CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF overcount the rank of an exactly uncontrollable or unobservable state (staircase.go controllabilityStaircase), and Reduce(ReduceUnobservable) is affected too. Cause: once a block passes fnorm > absFloor (tol*||A||), each singular value is compared only against the relative threshold tol*fnorm; there is no absolute floor per value. A block whose real part is about 1e-5 therefore counts rounding noise of about 1e-15 as rank. MATLAB uses an absolute default, n*norm(A,1)*eps, and gets this right. Repro (N=6, m=1, p=2, state 3 exactly unobservable): A=[197.11151535898398 -125.58165054554455 129.30370945971754 0 59.76947800347428 -5.265470231350326; -173.82085079604235 110.9846205585125 -114.44113190250626 0 -9.172863226049667 4.351756247287568; 136.7917714371087 -87.3782153938056 89.80570195554552 0 198.7113470934537 -4.207586106182046; 65.96476980969965 168.26520163148763 20.78475297333022 -0.31697863849222285 -106.39718338430359 188.40590032108176; 0 0 0 0 -0.15848931924611143 0; -35.79801621875614 23.572121758723704 -24.270765434267762 0 -196.34760124624893 -5.173930199602784], B=[0.5260775173811046; -0.01238866346289056; -0.9667981925794609; 0.3422733332214033; 0; 0.9601702866503661], C=[-4.3137684497061916e-07 -2.1079579943077972e-07 -8.568887533689471e-07 0 0.44660305575466125 9.931849187581927e-07; -9.111302618846769e-07 4.685166713003763e-07 -9.87479769908865e-07 0 0.4537233907250981 6.845466664428065e-07]. ObsvF(A,B,C,0) returns K=[2 2 2] (6 observable). Evidence that 5 is correct: the column for state 3 has zeros in C and in every other state's A row (exact structure from fzExtend), Obsv(A,C) has smallest singular value 3.3e-25, and ObsvF with tol 1e-14, 1e-12 or 1e-10 returns K=[2 2 1]. Abar shows noise of about 1e-15 in the unobservable coupling column being counted. Reduce(ReduceUnobservable) keeps 6 states on the same model; ReduceAll gives 4. Frequency: 4/2000 random FuzzCtrbF inputs on arm64 and 1/2000 on amd64, one of them CtrbF on a plain stiff plant: kind=0xae vals=[3 0 0.041993326592123736 0 -2.5862264388196863 0 0.6290414021982818 0.9141879810006508 0.687592153854844 -2.6945352201173414 -0.3240245478126962 -2 -2.934290568198731 0 -0.9801932348643629 0] (n=5, eig -5, -2e5, -5.5e-3, -220, -2.6e-3, condT 1.01, CtrbF K=[2 2 2] > 5). More ObsvF repros: kind=0x8c vals=[3 -1.2125755640793665 0 1.7804972689269993 0 -0.9732752605414227 -0.270240917348071 0.8868798792968446 -1 0 -3 0 1.2607636759098273 -1.8433242554233757 2.1906446725604654 2.3295988701096793] and kind=0xd6 vals=[-1.9267753943343813 -2.8464772362559905 -2.0951328559193296 -2.0601571048480407 0 -1 -1.1840262596694635 1.341242491997211 0.882534697639497 0.38794678127426163 0 -0.44674391775313427 -2.985434453550364 -0.07822883375954204 -1.3364640952854452 -1.2337450091041635]. Files: staircase.go, ctrbobsv.go, minimal.go, minreal_fuzz_test.go:438 (FuzzCtrbF). The GHNJYJ fix summary was cut off in my task text, so the implementer may already have filed this; coordinator should dedupe.

[w12f #45 fuzzstruct/review2] [controlsys, CORE/MATLAB parity] With the default tol=0, CtrbF/ObsvF set the rank threshold at n²·eps times each staircase block's own norm, not times ‖A‖. A rounding-noise singular value is then counted as rank once a block is small relative to ‖A‖, so the routine reports states that are structurally unobservable as observable. Repro: FuzzCtrbF kind=0xaa vals=[0 3 0.25 -83.7 59 -66 -60 0 0 -1 0.8 0 2 2.2 30 -1.3] (fzExtend: N=9, Ko=2, ‖A‖₂=2.07e4, condT 1.27). The reference SVD staircase on (Aᵀ,Cᵀ) has step block SVs [0.594, 6.94e-14]; 6.94e-14 is below eps·‖A‖ (4.6e-12). ObsvF(A,B,C,0) returns K=[2 2 2 2], sum 8, but the structural maximum is 7. MATLAB obsvf's default absolute tol (about 10·n·‖A‖₁·eps ≈ 6e-10) gives 7, and ObsvF(…,1e-10) also gives [2 2 2 1]. Files: ctrbobsv.go, staircase.go controllabilityStaircase (threshold := tol*fnorm).


Wave 13 attempt (branch fix/tf-wave13 commits 8c2ccf7 4a73116 aeac0be 2531f51) NOT merged; final review findings:

MinimalRealization / Reduce(ReduceAll) regressed from base-correct to non-minimal, keeping exactly unobservable states with unstable hidden eigenvalues (stable->unstable flip in the returned realization). Cause: scaleColumnsPow2 (staircase.go:106) scales each column of the first block toward ‖A‖. In Reduce's observability stage that block is Ccᵀ, taken from the controllability rotation. A column that is small because its large uncontrollable content was rotated out still carries noise at eps·‖C_full‖. Scaling that column up by about 2^9 lifts the noise above absFloor = n²eps‖Ac‖_F, which itself does not move, so in effect the test becomes relative per column rather than MATLAB's absolute default. The same mechanism applies to user CtrbF/ObsvF calls with a small, cancellation-derived column.
Repro (exact structure, no rotation, Ts=0.1, n=5,m=2,p=2): NewFromSlices(5,2,2, a=[0.8684323205674875 -0.6049616753433141 -0.817025610149589 0 0; 0 0.5112361371882209 -1.665579513685 0 0; 0 0.4426963353960824 2.2287867502570378 0 0; 1.450755586734131 0.5926180571361175 -1.003801815806515 -0.7392334214012152 2.598303245115053; 0.019516845706728403 0.7670269935617764 2.019276442042413 1.380736914734296 0.5174218017098235] (row-major), b=[0.7453432469816224 -0.1349637189736732; 0 0; 0 0; 0.2391746712711118 1.270569808451821; -1.6807270924517255 1.013393545638635], c=[0.10373234420450061 1.1189760895011407 -0.6387064209174134 0 0; 0.010176619760267125 -0.40735317004013655 0.15355429034927204 0 0], D=0, 0.1). Exact minimal order 1: states 1-2 have zero B rows and are never driven; states 3-4 have zero C columns and never feed states 0-2. Base 690c75a: MinimalRealization order 1, eig 0.868. Branch: order 3, eig {1.885, -2.106, 0.868}, two of them outside the unit circle. Response error is 4e-16, so only the order and stability are wrong. Same result on amd64. Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable) gives 3 (correct). Its Cc has singular values [0.104, 1.07e-16]: the noise SV is 65x below the branch's own absFloor of about 7e-15, yet ObsvF(RU) returns K=[2 1] at tol 0 and [1] at tol≥1e-14. Under MATLAB's absolute obsvf default (10·n·‖A‖₁·eps ≈ 3e-14) it would be rejected. Sweep: 2400 seeded Kalman-structured models (core plus uncontrollable and unobservable blocks, mostly orthogonally rotated) compared against the structural oracle. ReduceAll was base-correct and branch-wrong in 41 cases (6 of them plain O(1) rotated models, 2 exact unrotated). Reduced realization stable->unstable in 57 cases. The ObsvF/RO regression in case 1560 has the same cause. Same signature in cases 85/129/314/530: ObsvF(RU) K=[2 1] at tol 0, [1] at 1e-14. Disabling scaleColumnsPow2 alone (throwaway) cut the ReduceAll regressions from 41 to 9 and the unstable flips from 57 to 8. It also restored order 1 on the repro, but lost the tiny-B (JBKTCQ-type) fixes. So the tiny-B goal needs a mechanism that does not amplify noise columns, for example scaling only on raw user B, or an absolute floor that scales with the same factor.

TransferFunction regressed on models with ‖C‖≫‖A‖: the order rises and the denominator gains a nearly cancelled unstable pole (tfunst 0->1+ in 13/2400 sweep cases, all with C scaled by about 1e2-1e4). The 2531f51 row-stage floor max(n²,10n)·eps·‖A_stair‖_F (70·eps·‖A‖ at n=7) is about 2-3x below the noise left on structurally zero Hessenberg subdiagonals, which is 100-200·eps·‖A‖ on rotated models. Owner may downgrade this to informational: base was right only because its floor included ‖c‖, so it was not scale-robust.
Sweep case seed13/id55: continuous, n=7 (core 3, 2 uncontrollable, 2 unobservable, hidden blocks unstable), random orthogonal similarity, m=p=1, ‖A‖₂=6.03, ‖C‖=424. Base TF order 3, den [1 5.779 9.499 3.966] (stable, matches EvalFr). Branch TF order 5, den [1 7.2975 17.6727 14.9169 0.3165 -2.3821] with a positive real root, response error 1.9e-14. ObservabilityTol 1e-13 gives 5 and 3e-13 gives 3; it stays 3 up to 1e-6, so the gap is clear. Scaling C by 2^k: the branch gives 5 for every k in [-40,40]; base gives 5 for k≤-5, 3 for k in [0,20] and 2 at k=40. Other ids: 138 (6->10), 420, 507, 862, 880, 1297, 1575, 2127, 2157, 2166, 2210, 2335.

65BPNH (one rank rule; rounding-noise SVs must not count as rank): not met for Reduce's observability stage and for CtrbF/ObsvF on a B/C column that is small through cancellation. The per-column pow2 scaling makes noise SVs count again (blocking item 1, repro case 1571, Cc SVs [0.104, 1.07e-16] -> K=[2 1]). One rank rule fixing both directions is therefore not achieved: the tiny-B direction (PKUP2G/JBKTCQ) is bought by reopening the noise direction.

PKUP2G/65BPNH TF row stage: the scale-invariant subdiagonal floor (2531f51) is too tight for rotation noise of about 100-200·eps·‖A‖, so TF still counts noise subdiagonals and keeps hidden poles (blocking item 2). In the sweep, TF order is wrong in both base and branch in 502/2400 cases, mostly rotated models where the noise exceeds the floor.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #21] TransferFunction keeps rounding noise as states on block-structured MIMO models (not fixed, primary path unchanged by this branch; 65BPNH direction). Repro: n=10, m=2, p=2. A(i,i) = -(i+1); A(i,i+1) = 0.5 except A(4,5) = 0, so states 0-4 and 5-9 are decoupled. B(i, i/5) = 1+0.1i; C(i/5, i) = 1-0.05i; D=0; continuous. The staircase rotation likely turns exact zeros into rounding noise that the row observability stage counts as rank, the same mechanism 4a73116 fixed in Reduce. [w13 #23] Possible follow-up for the coordinator (a design gap, not a bug I found): TransferFunction has no structural (sminreal-style) pre-pass. When the rotation noise on a structurally zero subdiagonal is around 50-200·eps·‖A‖ (seen in models with diagonal scaling up to 10^±4, e.g. my sweep cases 5446 and 6438), no eps-scaled floor can drop it without also dropping real weak couplings. So structurally hidden states can still be kept and their poles land in the TF denominator. MATLAB-style structural elimination per output row (Sminreal already exists in sminreal.go) would remove them exactly. Left alone because it is outside this finding's scope.

[w13 #26] Reduce/CtrbF default tol is tighter than MATLAB. The default n²·eps·‖A‖_F is below MATLAB ctrbf's 10·n·‖A‖₁·eps (and minreal's documented sqrt(eps)) for small n. Repro: sweep-style plain model with exact structural hidden states, e.g. case 2320 (N=4, m=1, p=2, R=1): ReduceAll keeps 2 states because a noise singular value of 1.240e-15 is above the 1.226e-15 floor. Evidence: across 600 plain Gaussian models, ReduceAll over-counts 17 (2.8%) with the default and 6 with the MATLAB ctrbf tol, with no under-counts in any category. Files: staircase.go controllabilityStaircase, minimal.go Reduce. This is an owner/MATLAB-parity call, not strictly a pre-existing bug.


Wave 13 reports:

[w13 #27] MinimalRealization / Reduce(ReduceAll) regressed from base-correct to non-minimal, keeping exactly unobservable states with unstable hidden eigenvalues (stable->unstable flip in the returned realization). Cause: scaleColumnsPow2 (staircase.go:106) scales each column of the first block toward ‖A‖. In Reduce's observability stage that block is Ccᵀ, taken from the controllability rotation. A column that is small because its large uncontrollable content was rotated out still carries noise at eps·‖C_full‖. Scaling that column up by about 2^9 lifts the noise above absFloor = n²eps‖Ac‖_F, which itself does not move, so in effect the test becomes relative per column rather than MATLAB's absolute default. The same mechanism applies to user CtrbF/ObsvF calls with a small, cancellation-derived column.
Repro (exact structure, no rotation, Ts=0.1, n=5,m=2,p=2): NewFromSlices(5,2,2, a=[0.8684323205674875 -0.6049616753433141 -0.817025610149589 0 0; 0 0.5112361371882209 -1.665579513685 0 0; 0 0.4426963353960824 2.2287867502570378 0 0; 1.450755586734131 0.5926180571361175 -1.003801815806515 -0.7392334214012152 2.598303245115053; 0.019516845706728403 0.7670269935617764 2.019276442042413 1.380736914734296 0.5174218017098235] (row-major), b=[0.7453432469816224 -0.1349637189736732; 0 0; 0 0; 0.2391746712711118 1.270569808451821; -1.6807270924517255 1.013393545638635], c=[0.10373234420450061 1.1189760895011407 -0.6387064209174134 0 0; 0.010176619760267125 -0.40735317004013655 0.15355429034927204 0 0], D=0, 0.1). Exact minimal order 1: states 1-2 have zero B rows and are never driven; states 3-4 have zero C columns and never feed states 0-2. Base 690c75a: MinimalRealization order 1, eig 0.868. Branch: order 3, eig {1.885, -2.106, 0.868}, two of them outside the unit circle. Response error is 4e-16, so only the order and stability are wrong. Same result on amd64. Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable) gives 3 (correct). Its Cc has singular values [0.104, 1.07e-16]: the noise SV is 65x below the branch's own absFloor of about 7e-15, yet ObsvF(RU) returns K=[2 1] at tol 0 and [1] at tol≥1e-14. Under MATLAB's absolute obsvf default (10·n·‖A‖₁·eps ≈ 3e-14) it would be rejected. Sweep: 2400 seeded Kalman-structured models (core plus uncontrollable and unobservable blocks, mostly orthogonally rotated) compared against the structural oracle. ReduceAll was base-correct and branch-wrong in 41 cases (6 of them plain O(1) rotated models, 2 exact unrotated). Reduced realization stable->unstable in 57 cases. The ObsvF/RO regression in case 1560 has the same cause. Same signature in cases 85/129/314/530: ObsvF(RU) K=[2 1] at tol 0, [1] at 1e-14. Disabling scaleColumnsPow2 alone (throwaway) cut the ReduceAll regressions from 41 to 9 and the unstable flips from 57 to 8. It also restored order 1 on the repro, but lost the tiny-B (JBKTCQ-type) fixes. So the tiny-B goal needs a mechanism that does not amplify noise columns, for example scaling only on raw user B, or an absolute floor that scales with the same factor.

[w13 #28] TransferFunction regressed on models with ‖C‖≫‖A‖: the order rises and the denominator gains a nearly cancelled unstable pole (tfunst 0->1+ in 13/2400 sweep cases, all with C scaled by about 1e2-1e4). The 2531f51 row-stage floor max(n²,10n)·eps·‖A_stair‖_F (70·eps·‖A‖ at n=7) is about 2-3x below the noise left on structurally zero Hessenberg subdiagonals, which is 100-200·eps·‖A‖ on rotated models. Other ids: 138 (6->10), 420, 507, 862, 880, 1297, 1575, 2127, 2157, 2166, 2210, 2335.

title: CORE: Dare ill-conditioned R: extended pencil loses digits; residualTerms Inf on mat.Condition
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). #42 regressed vs 690c75a via 3b4de00 (BU6YAP). Fix hint: whiten inputs with ws.rChol.

[w13 #42 riccati/GEEI33] Dare extended pencil (3b4de00) loses digits when R is badly conditioned (R = D'D + eps*I with m > p), and Eig disagrees with trace(A-BK). Repro: go test -run 'FuzzRiccati/illcond_r_dare_(m3|cross)' (counted skip 'R ill-conditioned, extended pencil loses digits (known followup)'; drop the illR guard in mateq_fuzz_test.go to see the failures). Files: riccati.go (generalizedStableSubspace input-column QR, pencil mu balancing), testdata/fuzz/FuzzRiccati/illcond_r_dare_m3 and illcond_r_dare_cross. Evidence (300-bit Newton oracle): illcond_r_dare_m3 (kind 0x55, n=2, m=3, cond(R)=5.6e9) X relative error 1.1e-8 at 690c75a, 3.4e-6 at 95e7e75, 1.9e-7 now, against a 1-ulp perturbation change of 1.3e-15. illcond_r_dare_cross (kind 0x27, S=C'D, cond(R)=1.4e9, ||X||=1.8e-19): 9.5e-8 at 690c75a, 1.0 at 95e7e75, 2e-3 now, against 6e-7; Eig is off trace(A-BK) by 6e-6. Fix hint: whiten the inputs with the Cholesky factor already in ws.rChol (Btilde = B*U^-1, Stilde = S*U^-1, Rtilde = I). This is an equivalence transform, so X and the eigenvalues are unchanged (idare semantics kept), K = U^-1*Ktilde, and mu becomes ||Btilde||.

[w13 #49 riccati/review] riccati.go residualTerms returns Inf whenever mat.Solve reports a mat.Condition error, which gonum raises even though the result it computed is usable. With an ill-conditioned R+BᵀXB, a saved pass that was scored Inf loses every keepBest comparison against a later pass. The behaviour predates this branch and is left unfixed; the fix is to ignore mat.Condition there.

## Note (advisor, 2026-10-20)
This is a genuine wave 13 REGRESSION accepted under idare parity (3b4de00, Dare always uses the extended pencil). illcond_r_dare_cross went from 9.5e-8 at base to 2e-3, against an inherent sensitivity of 6e-7. Done-criterion: remove the illR guard in mateq_fuzz_test.go, so FuzzRiccati covers the case again and the fuzz target stops hiding the regression.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

title: CORE: internal-delay FreqResponse wrong near open-loop poles moved by delay loop (evalFrLFTInto)
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Fallback to frozen/closed-loop solve only on hard error; need ill-conditioning trigger. Distinct from HFKNLV.

[w13 #57 fuzz/MOI6LA] [EDGE] Internal-delay FreqResponse evaluates G11 + G12*Delta*(I - G22*Delta)^-1*G21 from the open-loop resolvent, so it loses about eps*cond(sI-A) relative accuracy where the delay loop moves a plant pole. The closed-loop condition is only about 25 there. Repro: FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay seed 15 (seed 7 with Tau=2 samples: discrete, dt=0.1, pair at |z|=1 with zeta=1e-8, b2 = first column of B, c2[i] = 0.5*sin(i+0.9)) at w=3.16227766: relative error 1.5e-8 against an exact solve of the A + Delta*b2*c2^T pencil. Continuous case: seed 2 (zeta=10^-9.5, w=sqrt(10), tau=0.3) gives 4.4e-8 relative. The discrete absorbed-state fallback (evalFrLFTInto) only triggers when I - H22*Delta is ill-conditioned, not when H itself is near a pole. Fix: solve the closed-loop pencil sI - A - B2*Delta*(I - D22*Delta)^-1*C2 directly when H is ill-conditioned.

[w13 #65 fuzz/review] Additional evidence for the existing reviewer followup, 'internal-delay FreqResponse loses accuracy at open-loop plant poles that the delay loop moves'. Files: frequency.go:775 evalFrLFTInto (open-loop H, then G11 + G12·Δ·(I − G22Δ)⁻¹·G21) and frequency_pole.go:372 evalFrLFTFrozenInto. The accurate frozen path is reached only when bd.evalInto errors, which it does not do for a near-zero or near-unit-circle pole. In the discrete case the absorbedSolver refine gate did not trigger. Repro A, continuous integrator at DC: fzDecode(t, 0x3a, [-20 -99.9 41 -45 60.333333333333336 -45 -26.666666666666668 -13.45 42 -10 -4.3757142857142854 8.666666666666666 -10 -163 -10 -0.05228787452803376]) gives n=1, m=2, p=3, A=[1e-13], tau=0.887, b2=B[:,0], c2=[0.3438]. At ω=0, s.System(t, fzSysOpts{Delays:true, Internal:true}).FreqResponse returns entry [3] = -80736 against an exact -80681.65 (rel 6.7e-4). All six entries are off by 1e-4 to 6.7e-4 relative. The closed-loop point condition is 1 and the oracle bound is 7.5e-9 to 2.7e-7, against misses of 1e2 to 5e2. Repro B, discrete: fzDecode(t, 0x41, [-4 85 0 33 0 0 -32 0 -2 -2.5 0.037 -13 36 -13 -60 -0.2614393726401688]) gives n=2, dt=0.01, eig 1±1e-6i, tau=1 sample. At ω=1.0000000001e-4 the result is -360400.8+2.35930e6i against an exact -378293.08+2.39261e6i (rel 1.56e-2, cond 2.79e6, bound 0.535, miss 3.8e4). The adjacent ω=1e-4 is correct to 1.5e-11. Oracle: exact rational solve of (xI − A − Δ·b2·c2ᵀ)X = B in fzFRInternalOracle. Fastest repro: go test -run XXX -fuzz FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay -fuzztime 60s . fails within about 1s. A 120s probe on the old code hid about 935 such misses at condOL=1, plus misses up to rel 0.3 at condOL ≥ 1e13.

[w13 #67 fuzz/review0] [EDGE] Internal-delay FreqResponse loses 7+ digits at an open-loop plant pole that the delay loop moves. This may already be filed by MOI6LA (its 'known:' skip reason); I could not confirm from the truncated summary. Files: frequency.go:775 evalFrLFTInto, frequency_pole.go:372 evalFrLFTFrozenInto. Mechanism: the code evaluates the open-loop H first and only falls back to the frozen closed-loop solve on a hard error, never when H is ill-conditioned. Repro 1 (continuous): run FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay with the fzFRCheckKnown skip disabled on kind=0x72 vals=[-0.6786402423930551 13 -0.8522801975522336 11.64528661442717 -40 9.730159100767608 -5.7124287797345685 0.8515788906023601 -1.8699414019192915 -0.9009541575928393 0.6904845230869261 -1.8615858804687453 0.37193006986806204 -10 -10 -0.9291681166465303]. That model is n=3, m=2, p=3, with an undamped pole at ω=0.2095847879716648 and tau about 0.118. At ω=0.2095847881812496 the relative error is 3.47e-7 (|Δ|=1.18e-7, |h|=0.339) against the exact big.Rat closed-loop solve, whose point condition is 8.52 and whose first-order bound is 6.7e-13. Repro 2 (discrete, worse): kind=0xd7 vals=[-0.8603088727097932 4.928966109060965 -0.5305909486010396 13 -1.7603256926868887 13 5.5794598346733535 -0.5028651286615842 -1.6756909102435067 -9.522762649906602 -1.2934801749704727 -2.8222193382401946 0.1393351192955018 -10 -0.4596958443663803 0.02128779065627474]. That model is n=6, m=3, p=3, dt=0.0211, with pole pairs within 1e-5 of z=1. At ω=0.017364980811526754 the relative error is 1.27e-4 (|Δ|=1.68e-4, |h|=1.32) at closed-loop condition 1.43e4, with bound 2.6e-9. Both discrepancies are far above float64 rounding of the given coefficients. Suggested fix direction: switch to evalFrLFTFrozenInto when the open-loop solve is ill-conditioned (large H22 or a large residual), not only when it errors.

[w13 #68 fuzz/review1] [EDGE/CORE-ish] Internal-delay FreqResponse returns wrong values when the frequency point sits on a lightly damped open-loop pole but the closed loop is well conditioned. Repro: go test -run=FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay with kind=0x41, vals=[-4 85 0 33 0 0 -32 0 -2 -2.5 0.037 -13 36 -13 -60 -0.2614393726401688]. This decodes to discrete dt=0.01, n=2, open-loop eig 1-5e-13 ± 1e-6i, internal delay tau=1 sample with b2=B and c2=0.5·sin(i-13), input delay 20, evaluated at ω=1.0000000001e-4. Library gives -360400.814+2359303.208i. The exact closed-loop value is -378293.080+2392607.289i, from a big.Rat solve of (zI−A−Δb2c2ᵀ)X=B times z^-20, which I re-derived independently with Python Fractions. That is a relative error of 1.6%, while the closed-loop condition is only 2.8e6. Cause: evalFrLFTInto (frequency.go:775-831) builds G11+G12Δ(1−G22Δ)⁻¹G21 from an open-loop solve with |G22|≈1.8e14. The bdSolver succeeds, so the frozen/closed-loop fallback is never taken, and the discrete refine gate xMax·(1+loopMax) > refineCondition·rhsMax does not fire. A plain complex128 LFT gives the same wrong value.

[w13 #69 fuzz/review2] [CORE] Discrete internal-delay FreqResponse returns a silently wrong finite value at a lightly damped open-loop pole. Repro: fzDecode(t, 0x41, [-3, 13, 0, 0, 77, 0, 0, 0, -2, -10, 0.37, -77, -10, -300, 72, -0.1307196863200844]) then s.System(t, fzSysOpts{Delays:true, Internal:true}). That gives n=2, m=p=1, dt=0.01, A=[0.9999999999499999 9.999999999777057e-06; -9.999999999727683e-06 0.9999999999499998], B=[-0.22547187812891345; -0.9990597137251606], C=[5.417961692372929e-07 -9.70531651649883e-07], D=0, and an internal delay of 1 sample with b2=B, c2=[-0.4997600792903656 -0.28305381844909017]. Call FreqResponse at w=0.001000000001 (the resonance times 1+1e-9). arm64 returns (0 - 1.944601535797119e-06i); amd64 returns (-2.235e-08 - 1.93715e-06i). The exact value is (-1.1938325831196937e-08 - 1.935222691114017e-06i): the real part is wrong by 100% (arm64) or about 87% (amd64), and |Δ|/|h| is 0.78% on arm64. Two independent references agree on the exact value. One is the exact big.Rat solve of the absorbed 3-state model [[A, b2],[c2ᵀ, 0]] at the library's z. The other is the library's own FreqResponse of that absorbed explicit model, which matches to 1e-15. The closed loop is well conditioned (cond about 3e5), so this is not a precision limit. The open-loop point is singular to working precision (cond 2.4e14), and evalFrLFTInto (frequency.go:775) keeps the H-then-LFT result. Neither the bd.evalInto error nor the discrete refineCondition check sends it to absorbedSolver or evalFrLFTFrozenInto. Files: frequency.go (evalFrLFTInto, absorbedSolver) and frequency_pole.go (evalFrLFTFrozenInto). FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay finds it within 2000 execs.

title: DECISION: TunePID |S|<=4 / 58.5deg PM bar for undelayed first designs (PD |S| 17 near z=1)
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). tuneAt(wc0,...,robust=false) bounds |S| only with delay; V2AYQB exposes it on near-unit plants. Owner: apply Pidtune bar to TunePID all families?

[w13 #4 pidtune/V2AYQB] TunePID: an undelayed first-pass design has no |S| bound. Repro: dt 0.01, num 10*{2.761969998249568e-16, 2.6332895798497864e-16, 6.196985260193668e-17}, den {1,-5.388323209156541,12.045405202918547,-14.292531743733242,9.488502158799133,-3.339413745774066,0.486361336946173}; TunePID PD with PIDTuningOptions{} returns Kp 0.5639 and Kd -1.667e5, PM 63, with oracle |S| 16.9 inside the reported band (17.04 at 7.7e-4 rad/s with the plant evaluated in 256-bit). Pidtune PD on the same plant gives Kp 0.9985, Kd 1.009e4, Tf 1010. Cause: tuneAt(wc0, gainSign, tau > 0, false) only bounds |S| when the plant has a delay (pid_tuning.go TunePID default path). Base returned an error on this plant, so this is a new value of low robustness, not a regression of a correct value.

[w13 #6 pidtune/V2AYQB] Observation, not a bug: TunePID free I or free P accepts the plant's margin at wc0 when |S| <= 4, as documented. The IP3XIC k=10 plant (above) with I returns PM 28.7 deg and |S| 2.24; GK5SUC A with P returns 45.7 deg, same on base. The coordinator should decide whether the owner's 58.5 deg bar applies to TunePID as well as Pidtune.

[w13 #8 pidtune/review2] Title: TunePID PD can return |S| 17 inside its own analysis band on near-z=1 plants (pre-existing: the first design at wc0 is not |S|-bounded for undelayed plants). Repro: num {2.761969998249568e-15, 2.6332895798497864e-15, 6.196985260193668e-16}, den {1,-5.388323209156541,12.045405202918547,-14.292531743733242,9.488502158799133,-3.339413745774066,0.486361336946173}, Dt 0.01, StateSpace(), then TunePID(ctx, sys, PidtunePD, PIDTuningOptions{}). It returns Kp 0.5639, Kd -166694 (gains of opposite sign, since gainSign is 0 once the integrator is recognised) at PM 63 deg. The |S| peak is 17.0 at w=7.7e-4, inside FrequencyBand [4.95e-8, 4.95e-4 x...] (in-band peak 16.9); stability is exact Schur-stable. A second case, nearunit plant num {-5.917373360562065e-16,-3.1176768703785916e-16}, den {1,-3.9985941793495767,5.995783163531163,-3.99578378890103,0.9985948047194504}, Dt 0.01, PD: |S| 6.31 in band. Base also returns |S|>4 TunePID PD/PDF/PIDF designs on ordinary plants. Cause: pid_tuning.go TunePID calls tuneAt(wc0, gainSign, tau > 0, false), so robust is false without a delay. V2AYQB now exposes this on near-unit plants, and its test only checks |S| for P/I. Owner call whether TunePID should bound |S| <= pidTuningMaxSensitivity for all families. Files: pid_tuning.go (TunePID tuneAt robust flag), pid_tuning_fallback_test.go.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-20): apply |S| <= 4 to every TunePID family; no 58.5° PM floor
Rationale: TunePID's own contract already accepts the margin at wc0 only when |S| <= 4. The robust = tau > 0 asymmetry, which skips the |S| check on undelayed plants, has no justification. The 58.5° floor is Pidtune policy; TunePID is the explicit-target tool, the same philosophy as V7UW3M (explicit wc ungated).
- (a) Read tuneAt first. If robust=true also triggers back-off or search, add only the |S| check.
- (b) On |S| failure, return the same error shape the delayed path returns today: PIDTuningError wrapping unattainable, with the |S| value.
- (c) In the sweep, a base design with |S| > 4 that becomes an error is an allowed flip. A base design with |S| <= 4 that flips is BLOCKING.
- Separate smell to investigate: the PD gets opposite-sign gains (Kp 0.5639, Kd -1.667e5) because gainSign becomes 0 once the integrator is recognised.

title: EDGE: ReduceUnobservable/ReduceAll return rotated model when nothing removed (pole flips)
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Extend 4a73116 unrotated-model fix. Low severity.

[w13 #25 tf/review0] ReduceUnobservable (and ReduceAll when ncont<n) returns an orthogonally rotated model even when the observability stage removes nothing. title: EDGE: HinfSyn false 'P21(z=1) not full row rank' for discrete pole within 1e-14 of z=1
body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Passes at A=1, 1-1e-12; H2Syn fine. Rank-test tolerance.

[w12f #5 fuzzmat/SWTCHJ] HinfSyn reports a rank-deficient P21(z=1) for a discrete pole within about 1e-14 of z=1 [EDGE]. Files: hinfsyn.go (handling of modes near z=±1). Repro: fuzz tuple kind=0x31 vals=[-10 1 -31 4 -24 -37 0 39 -783 -1.6666666666666667 -57.63 0 -10 -10 -10 -10], then fzDecode, syNormC and syRegPlant (n=1, m=1, p=3, dt=1e-4, B=[-0.9667981925794609], C=[-1.0153621182995027 -1.1701046921324967 -0.7745287458654208], D=[-38.51171102644574 38.865141783905486 -36.96114248311336], rho=sigma=0.01). title: CORE: Sigma small singular values from Gram eigenvalues lose accuracy (sqrt(eps)*sigma1)
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13).

[w13 #55 fuzz/MOI6LA] [CORE-ish] Sigma loses accuracy on small singular values. complexSVDWorkspace takes them from eigenvalues of the Gram matrix G^H*G (frequency_svd.go: fillBlock, singularValues), so the absolute error is about sqrt(eps)*sigma1 instead of eps*sigma1. Repro: FuzzFreqResponse seed 7 (discrete, n=4, m=p=2, dt=0.1, pair at |z|=1 with zeta=1e-8) at w=3.16227766: sys.Sigma and FRD.Sigma give sigma2=3.1155e-6, exact 1.2382e-6 (fzSingularValues via gonum SVD), sigma1=224.9. The relative error is about eps*(sigma1/sigma2)^2, so it is fully wrong once sigma1/sigma2 > 1e8. MATLAB sigma uses svd. Fix: complex SVD (e.g. a Golub-Kahan step on the 2x2 case) instead of Gram eigenvalues.

title: Fuzz testing across controlsys
body:
Coverage-guided Go fuzz targets (testing.F) across controlsys, each checking soundness against an independent oracle.
Crash = wrong value/verdict, unstable design returned, panic, error-contract breach. Documented unsupported/unattainable = t.Skip. Seed corpus = closed ergo repros; crashers committed under testdata/fuzz. Run -fuzz locally per wave (scripts/fuzz.sh), replay under amd64 before filing; not in CI.
Foundation task first; the rest depend on it.

title: CORE: Nyquist RHPZerosCL undercounts delayed-loop windings once wc*tau >~ 12 (darg aliasing)
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Stability verdict unaffected; count wrong.

[w13 #66 fuzz/review] Nyquist RHPZerosCL undercounts windings of delayed loops once wc*tau >~ 12. Repro: sys,_ := NewFromSlices(1,1,1,[]float64{-1},[]float64{1},[]float64{50},[]float64{0},0); sys.SetInputDelay([]float64{1}); r,_ := sys.Nyquist(nil,0) gives RHPZerosCL=12. True count is 16: a dense 4M-point winding of 1+L on [0,1e5] and fzQuasiRHP agree. k=100 gives 16 vs 32; k<=20 is correct. Files: nyquist.go continuousHalf / nyquistPath.piece. segment uses about 10 points per decade, and piece bisects only when |darg(1+L)| > pi/4. Because darg is taken mod 2pi, a delay rotation of more than pi per base step aliases while |L|>1. Second suspected mechanism, not isolated: for D!=0 loops the early return `if p.sys.HasDelay() && closure != 0 { return nil }` skips the tail beyond wHi=1e3*max(|p|,1/tau). The stability verdict is unaffected (the count stays >0); only the number is wrong. In the fuzz this is gated by the narrow skip 'known: Nyquist aliases delay windings...' (fzFRSeeds last seed).

title: CORE: HinfNorm accuracy misses documented 1e-10 (under-report up to 3.6e-4, race-build 3e-10)
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Race-build case (test now skips it under race): HinfNorm slow-resonance model decoded under -race build is 3e-10 low vs 1e-10 contract: fzSeed{N:3,M:1,P:1,Mag:{-8,4},Damp:{2.5,1},Shear:-10,Rot:0.37,no delays} in TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go). Re-enable under race once fixed. Common suspects: norms.go certifyPeak treating sub-probe candidates as no crossing, hasImagEigs nearAxisTol on stiff unbalanced pencils (Dggbal before Dggev), peak search missing narrow humps, sigmaEvaluator over-report.

[w12 #68 linalg/LASTBLOCK] The new test TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go, 5YUZIK) fails under -race, which CI runs. It is deterministic and does not skip when raceEnabled.
`go test -race -count=2 -run TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle .` on fed3cf1 (arm64) fails both times: "norms_test.go:2044: slow resonance: HinfNorm = 239.388723153999, oracle 239.388723226662 (rel -3.04e-10)". assertHinfNormMatchesOracle allows 1e-10 relative (norms_test.go:1854). Without -race it passes on arm64 and on amd64. In the race build fzDecode produces slightly different A data, and on that model the norm is 3e-10 low, against a documented accuracy of 1e-10. Base is 30% low on the same model, so this is a CI test failure, not a value regression. Fix: either reach 1e-10 on that data, or skip/loosen only under raceEnabled.

[w12 #74 fuzz/XQYP43] HinfNorm/Norm(Inf) under-reports a lightly damped discrete peak near z=1 by about 3.6e-4 relative, although norms.go peakGain documents certification to 1e-10. The result is still within MATLAB's default 1e-2 tolerance, so parity holds; the library's own claim is what's breached. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=[0.9999999959758767 5.3457259458380696e-09 -1.3269470226717082e-08 0.9999999927772968], B=[-0.6656134553337595 0.5410494509487578], C=[-999097.8260547261 363185.4084160624], D=[-736.7935074839925], dt=1e-4). HinfNorm gives 9.467722253631506e13 at ω=8.685e-5; the exact rational response gives 9.471110502171495e13 at ω=8.8388e-5. A naive float LU sweep agrees with the exact value to 1e-15, and the backward-error sensitivity is about 1e-7, so this is a search or certification miss, not conditioning. The exact γ-crossing test confirms a crossing at norm·(1+1e-6). Fuzz tuple: FuzzHinfNorm kind=0x41 vals=[-4 2.25 0.5 -145 -26 18 34 5629.5 -8 -0.3 1.1 32 1044 -0.5 0.2 -10]. The MIMO variant kind=0x5b with the same vals is also low by 3.6e-4. Suspect: norms.go peakGain/certifyPeak/upperBound. The rule 'candidates whose evaluated gains stay below the probe count as no crossing' probably certifies falsely when the candidate ω is off the true peak (2.5% off here).

[w12 #78 fuzz/review0] HinfNorm/linfNorm under-reports the peak gain of a stable, stiff, symmetric continuous SISO model by 2.1e-4 relative. This is present at base 2e4a07d (the base FuzzHinfNorm fails on the same input). Repro: put a corpus file `go test fuzz v1` / byte('À') / float64 vals 39,0,0.3,0,-0.2,0,0,0,0,-9.5,2.5,-76,-10,-10,-10,-10 into testdata/fuzz/FuzzHinfNorm/x, then run `go test -run FuzzHinfNorm/x .`. The decoded model has n=6, m=p=1, D=0, condT=1 (symmetric A, ‖A‖≈2e6) and stable eigenvalues {-0.00316, -0.00998, -50, -126, -399, -2e6}. HinfNorm returns 4.865840926965868e-05 at ω=0.003992. The exact big.Rat σmax at ω=0.0038510 is 4.86684164441442e-05. The expected error bound is fzNormTol ≈ 1e-6, so the peak search misses a low-frequency hump between the two slow poles. Files: hinfnorm.go (HinfNorm/linfNorm peak search). Evidence: hinfnorm_fuzz_test.go:78 fails on base and :50 on the branch; norms_fuzz_test.go:113 also fails.

data.title: CORE: ZPK sortConjugatePairs doubles pair when negative-imag root first; C2D matched wrong
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Root: zpk.go:322 sortConjugatePairs. #47 is the public C2D matched symptom; after the fix remove the FuzzC2DMatched known-defect skip (discretize_fuzz_test.go:644). Cross-ref 2NVSQQ (different ZPK.TransferFunction defect).

[w14 #44 fuzz/4UAU4O] [CORE] ZPK->TF doubles a conjugate pole/zero pair when the negative-imaginary root is listed first. Repro: NewZPK(nil, []complex128{-1i, 1i}, 1, 0) then transferFunction() gives den [1 0 2 0 1], want [1 0 1]. Poles [-1-2i, -1+2i] give [1 4 14 20 25], want [1 2 5]; (+,-) order is correct. Public symptom: ZPK.StateSpace() returns 4 states and D=0 for a biproper 2-pole ZPK. File zpk.go:322 sortConjugatePairs: it conjugates r to positive imag, then searches k>i for conjR, which is root i itself, finds nothing, appends a pair, and the partner later appends a second pair. Downstream, C2D(matched) breaks whenever a complex root has sin(|Im lambda|*Ts)<0 (an undersampled resonance, omega*Ts>pi, maps the pair to negative-imag-first). Either the value is wrong (corpus testdata/fuzz/FuzzC2DMatched/7aeb2715bda38a0a: Hd(1)=36.40 vs Hc(0)=77.95, 4 states instead of 2) or a correct case becomes an error, 'transfer function is improper' (corpus 16fa0a88fe333983). After the fix, remove the known-defect skip in FuzzC2DMatched (discretize_fuzz_test.go) so both corpus files become regression tests.

[w14 #47 fuzz/review0] [CORE] C2D matched returns a wrong value with nil error when a complex pole aliases (|Im p|·Ts in (π, 2π)). Repro: G = 16.01/(s²+0.2s+16.01) (poles −0.1±4j) as NewFromSlices(2,1,1,[0 1 -16.01 -0.2],[0 1],[16.01 0],[0],0), then C2D(Ts=1, C2DOptions{Method: C2DMethodMatched}). EvalFr(z=1) returns 0.3332, but the matched method must preserve DC gain G(0)=1 (MATLAB c2d 'matched' does). At z=e^{0.3i} it returns 0.307−0.163i vs oracle K(z+1)/((z−p1)(z−p2)) = 1.0017−0.1702i with p=e^{(−0.1±4j)Ts}. Ts=1.2 is also wrong (DC 0.613); Ts=0.5 is correct. FuzzC2DMatched skips this as 'ZPK conjugate ordering defect'. Files: conversion_plan.go and the matched/ZPK path.

data.title: CORE: Nyquist finite RHPZerosCL for delayed neutral loops |D|>=1; error class at wc*tau>1e5
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Common theme: Nyquist error contract for delayed loops it cannot count. #36 returns garbage counts (should be ErrDelayUnsupported or documented error); #41 is optional error-class cleanup.

[w14 #36 delayfreq/review] Nyquist returns a finite RHPZerosCL for delayed loops with |D| >= 1, which have infinitely many closed-loop RHP roots. This is already wrong on base 0c02feb, so not a regression from this branch, and I did not fix it. Repro: quasiLoop{num: {d, d*a1+0.3k, d*a0+k}, den: {1, a1, a0}, tau} with k=1.8749, a1=2.6223, a0=0.25411, d=1.49706, tau=0.71947 (input delay, controllable-canonical realization like quasiLoop.system in delay_nyquist_test.go). With L(j∞) = D, |D| > 1 and a delay, the closed loop is a neutral system whose roots approach Re s = ln|D|/τ > 0, so no finite count is correct. Branch I/O form returns 578 with no error (base 68). The PullDelaysToLFT form returns ErrDelayUnsupported on the branch and ErrSingularTransform on base. More cases from the same PCG(3,5) sweep: d=1.269, τ=2.713 gives 996; d=1.427, τ=2.950 gives 840; d=1.0144, τ=2.225 gives 5200. Files: nyquist.go (continuousHalf tail when HasDelay && closure != 0; nyquistEncirclements). Suggested: return ErrDelayUnsupported, or another documented error, when |D| >= 1 and the loop is delayed, following MATLAB semantics.

[w14 #41 delayfreq/review2] Optional, low priority. Nyquist on loops with wc*tau above about 1e5 reports ErrSingularTransform ('1+L = 0 on the contour') rather than a count or ErrDelayUnsupported, even within the 2^21 sample budget. Repro: L = 33894/(s+18.92)*e^{-5.23s}, built with NewFromSlices(1,1,1,{-18.92},{1},{33894},{0},0) and SetInputDelay({5.23}); the error comes from Nyquist(nil,0). Cause: the asymptotic closed-loop roots near |s| of about k have Re s at most about 2*pi/(k*tau^2), roughly 7e-6 here, which is about 1e-10 relative and inside the library's on-contour tolerance. The branch's count is not wrong, and base returned a count (1242) that is wrong by about 45x against the true value of about 5.6e4. The only issue is the error type; MATLAB's nyquist does not count encirclements. File it only if a clearer error class is wanted (files: nyquist.go refine and the at() on-contour check).

data.title: CORE: DiskMargin too-small Alpha at w=+Inf for parallel delays with odd-integer delay ratio
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14).

[w14 #45 fuzz/PN4IYP] CORE: DiskMargin reports a too-small Alpha (too-large ‖S−½‖∞ and Ms) at ω=+Inf for parallel delayed paths whose delay ratio is an odd integer. Repro (public API): G=NewGain([[0.3]]); G.SetInputDelay([0.5]); K=NewGain([[-0.25]]); K.SetInputDelay([1.5]); L=Parallel(G,K); DiskMargin(L) -> 1/Alpha=1.722222 at ω=+Inf. L is periodic in ω, so the exact value is the sup over φ of |1/(1+0.3e^{-jφ}-0.25e^{-j3φ}) - 1/2| = 1.179565 (dense sweep; closed loop stable). With G = NewFromSlices(1,1,1,[-1],[1],[0.1],[0.3]) instead of the static gain: 1.722222@+Inf vs exact 1.238437@ω=4.486. k=3 and k=5 are wrong; k=2 and k=4 are correct. 1.722222 = |1+0.55|/(2·0.45) is the sup over independent phases (L = -0.3-0.25), which looks like a bound on the incommensurate torus or on the tail being reported as the value. GetDelayModel(L) gives tau=[2h,h] cascaded with D22≠0. HinfNorm(Feedback(L,nil,-1)) is correct on the same model (0.73285 vs exact 0.732846), so the fault is in DiskMargin's delay-loop path. data.title: EDGE: Nyquist RHPPoles hides unstable pole ~1.03 beside huge pole (boundary tol ~ sqrt(eps)*max|p|)
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Common root: classifyNyquistBoundary/poleStabilityTolerance scale with spectral radius; sys.Poles() is correct. Stops FuzzFreqResponse within minutes.

[w14 #35 delayfreq/WYLHSA] Pre-existing, numerically extreme, but it stops FuzzFreqResponse within 1-3 minutes: Nyquist RHPPoles is 1 where the fuzz oracle expects 2, for discrete 2-state loops with eig(A) about {1.0018, 5.5e9}. Repro: FuzzFreqResponse inputs kind=0x41 vals=[0.3 -0.25 52 126 58 0 5.5 49 -1 -10 51.37 -15 88 152 74 10] and vals=[0.3 -0.20833333333333334 45 -38 0 0 5.5 0 -1 -80 0.37 0 -50 -10 -10 -10] (dt=0.1); both fail on 0c02feb. Cause: classifyNyquistBoundary puts every pole within sqrt(eps)*max|p| (about 82 here) on the boundary, so it hides a pole 1.8e-3 outside the unit circle. fzNyqPoleClass treats that pole as clearly unstable even though its error band is much wider. Files: nyquist.go classifyNyquistBoundary, nyquist_fuzz_test.go fzNyqPoleClass. Either the library or the fuzz harness needs to change; that call is yours.

[w14 #37 delayfreq/review0] [EDGE, pre-existing on 0c02feb] Nyquist reports RHPPoles=1 for a discrete model with two exactly unstable poles. FuzzFreqResponse hits this in under a minute: kind=0x41 vals=[0.03 -0.8333333333333334 -51 0 0 0 98.5 0 -0.1 -10 -44.9075 -17 -10 -10 -10 -60], failing at nyquist_fuzz_test.go:189 ('intended off-boundary unstable'). data.title: EDGE: test oracles sweepOracle/fzQuasiRHP undercount RHP roots of neutral quasi-polynomials (D!=0)

Second case: num=[-0.4873935496838586 238.2482872956028 676.9561718253274], den=[1 -14.048506952489628 4.371096488549578], tau=3.6253950291690042 gives 298 against 316. This could produce false failures in the fuzz Nyquist checks for D≠0 loops.

[w14 #38 delayfreq/review0] [TEST ORACLE, low priority] The fzQuasiRHP test helper (fuzz_helpers_test.go:834) returns ok=true with count 1 for a neutral loop where the argument principle gives 133, and the branch Nyquist also gives 133. The loop: ord-2 stable den, num = d*(s+zr)^2 with |d| in [0.1,0.9] and zr in [10,1000], tau=1.521. I did not save the exact num/den: the replay to print them was refused and the scratch dir is deleted. The helper likely truncates its search region for D!=0 (neutral) loops. data.title: DECISION: Reduce/MinimalRealization defaults: Equalize prescaling and Tol (sqrt(eps) vs ctrbf floor)
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). MATLAB minreal prescales and documents tol=sqrt(eps); current default is no Equalize and ctrbf floor 10*n*||A||_1*eps. Measured trade-offs below.

[w14 #3 tf/PKUP2G 65BPNH] Reduce on badly scaled models without Equalize: in the Kalman sweep at d=4 (state scales 10^±4, KALMAN_SWEEP_DIAG=4 KALMAN_SWEEP_N=4000), 65/4000 reduced realizations have response error >1e-6 (base 171). With Equalize forced on: d=4 response 171 fixed / 1 regressed, order 92 regressed; d=0 order 477 fixed / 15 regressed. Owner decision: default prescaling, as MATLAB minreal prescales. Files: minimal.go Reduce/equalize.

[w14 #9 tf/review1] Owner parity question: Reduce/MinimalRealization use the ctrbf floor (10·n·||A||₁·eps) rather than MATLAB minreal's documented sqrt(eps). On my sweep, 82 Kalman-structured over-counts (most with hidden unstable states kept) resolve with Tol 1.8-3.2x the default, and all resolve below sqrt(eps)-scale tolerances without any under-count. The branch's doc gives the counter-case (weakly coupled slow plants). Files: minimal.go ReduceOpts.Tol, staircase.go ctrbfFloor.

[w14 #5 tf/review] Owner decision, Reduce default Tol (review item 6): MATLAB minreal documents tol = sqrt(eps). Measured with that default: TestReduceIssue26PIPlantLoop drops to order 1; KALMAN_SWEEP_DIAG=3 gives 174 under-counts and 277 response errors (base 9); with Equalize forced there are still O(1) response errors at the correct order (e.g. rr=4.71 on id 1185 and 12.5 on id 1609, seed PCG(id, 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15), kB=8). Kept n²·eps plus the ctrbf floor. Files: minimal.go Reduce, staircase_sweep_test.go.

data.title: DECISION: TunePID PD mixed-sign gains on integrating plants (pidTuningDCSign returns 0)
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Cross-ref FRD wrong-sign task (stable plants, real instability) — this one is stable designs, sign policy only.

[w14 #14 pidtune/SIVH4J] TunePID PD returns gains of opposite sign on integrating plants. Repro: TransferFunc num {8.2}, den {1,-1}, Dt 0.05, then StateSpace and TunePID(ctx, sys, PidtunePD, PIDTuningOptions{}). It returns Kp 0.0344, Kd -0.0019; with PhaseMargin 30 it returns Kp 0.0273, Kd -0.0036. Pidtune PD on the same plant gives same-sign gains (Kp 0.0378, Kd +3.1e-4, Tf 8.2e-4), and MATLAB pidtune never gives mixed signs. IP3XIC k=10 PD does the same (fix: Kp 0.79, Kd -1.23e5). The designs are stable with |S| <= 4, so this is about the sign policy, not robustness. Cause: pidTuningDCSign returns 0 once Pidtune recognises an integrator, so pidTuningSignConsistent accepts any mix of signs (pid_tuning.go, pidTuningDCSign and pidTuningSignConsistent; TunePID default PD path). Owner call: whether integrating plants should require same-sign gains, perhaps using the sign of the integrator's residue. Note SIVH4J's new test pins two such mixed-sign PD designs as acceptable for |S|.

data.title: PERF: TF 2x slower on zero-diagonal models; gonum Dlasrt allocs in FRD Sigma/PeakGain
data.body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Owner-deferred perf. #11 Dlasrt fix belongs in the gonum repo (plantcontrol.org/v1/gonum lapack/gonum/dlasrt.go); cross-ref from controlsys.

[w14 #8 tf/review1] Perf: TransferFunction on zero-diagonal models (Padé, companion and chain realizations) is now about 2x slower (BenchmarkTransferFunction/pade18 2.14x), because the response check and the Osborne re-conversion run per structural row group. A possible mitigation is one tfCheck shared across groups, or a cheaper gate than any zero on the diagonal. Files: transfer.go convert, convertRowGroups, newTFCheck.

[w14 #11 norms/review0] [gonum] Dlasrt allocates on every decreasing sort. lapack/gonum/dlasrt.go:34 calls sort.Sort(sort.Reverse(sort.Float64Slice(d))), which costs 2 heap allocs per call: one to box the slice into an interface, one for the Reverse wrapper. Dlasq1 calls it at its end, so controlsys FRD.Sigma and FRD.PeakGain (complexSVDWorkspace.singularValues via impl.Dlasq1 on fix/norms-wave14) now allocate 2x the number of frequencies. Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 0c02feb -candidate fix/norms-wave14 -bench 'BenchmarkFRDSigma_MIMO_2000|BenchmarkFRDPeakGain_MIMO_2000'. Allocs go from 8 to 4012 and from 6 to 4010; B/op goes from 67.9k to 148k and from 2.3k to 82.7k. Fix in gonum: slices.Sort followed by an in-place reverse, or slices.SortFunc with a descending comparator. Files: plantcontrol.org/v1/gonum@v0.20.6 lapack/gonum/dlasrt.go.

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The A solve fails (cond 1.4e21) and poleSpacing near=true (pole -1.88e-8). DCGain returns +9.684e11. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Example dc9: a continuous upper-triangular A with diagonal entries -2.89e-5, -3.09e-11, -1.75e-5, ... gives DCGain [-Inf, -78626.6], while FreqResponse(0) and the exact big.Rat solve give [-1.1129e18, -3.0967e18]. Another: discrete 2x2 A=[0.9998853776327908 0.0001224178710512369; -6.299779160740249e-05 1.000067282291557], B=[-0.7525840543357618 -1.8936563902987011; -0.3336326973535324 -0.8822404525470022], C=[-1.3323341784633906 -0.2326700817740477; 0.48991627788123343 0.8587983672300241], dt=0.01. Its DCGain is finite but has relative error 5e-5 against the exact value (789372732529716 vs 789410222466333), and FreqResponse(0) is +Inf in every entry. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). DCGain[1,0] = 6.73e13; exact rational limit on the float model is +Inf (det(I-A) = 0 exactly, exact pole order 1, computed eigenvalue 2e-15 from 1). The value comes from dcGainByStructuralEntries. dcGainByBlockLaurent declines because it needs a 1x1 block with A_kk == x0, although the branch's exactDetIsZero could detect this block. Files: response.go dcGainByStructuralEntries / dcGainByBlockLaurent.

[w12f #31] CORE: DCGain returns a finite value for an exact integrator, so Bandwidth returns +Inf, nil instead of ErrInvalidArgument. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1,A=[-1000 10; 0 0], b=[1;1], c=[1 1], d=0). Exact residue at s=0 is 1.01, so the DC gain is infinite (MATLAB dcgain gives Inf). [w14 #2] FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 (‖A‖≈4e43) passes only by luck. TF keeps the z=1 integrator only through the ‖c‖-relative test for c being zero. The kept Cc≈4e29 against ‖A‖≈4e43 is rotation noise; a ‖c‖-free full-model c-test drops it and DCGain becomes 0 instead of ±Inf (seen on this branch's interim TF variant). Needs a non-polynomial integrator residue in response.go dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit/dcGainByDecoupledSingularModes for row-decoupled z=1 or s=0 states: residue [C_r(λI-A_rr)^-1 A_rk + c_k]·b_k (w13 #19). No wave-14 track owns response.go.

Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

Perf (CR7GLM, caused by AUOTFB): newPidtuneGate now runs on every automatic Pidtune call. It evaluates the plant about 3000 times (sens grid about 230 points/decade, cross grid 100/decade, no shared points, band floor*1e-3 to wc*1e3). Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.

Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0x80, [0,3,0.3,4,0,0,6,0,-1,-3,0.8,-3.5,-10,52,-10,-10]) gives modes ζ=0.1 at 1 rad/s and ζ=0.01 at 2 rad/s, with a 19.95 s output delay. With Equalize forced on: d=4 response 171 fixed / 1 regressed, order 92 regressed; d=0 order 477 fixed / 15 regressed. Owner decision: default prescaling, as MATLAB minreal prescales. [w14 #9 tf/review1] Owner parity question: Reduce/MinimalRealization use the ctrbf floor (10·n·||A||₁·eps) rather than MATLAB minreal's documented sqrt(eps). On my sweep, 82 Kalman-structured over-counts (most with hidden unstable states kept) resolve with Tol 1.8-3.2x the default, and all resolve below sqrt(eps)-scale tolerances without any under-count. The branch's doc gives the counter-case (weakly coupled slow plants). Files: minimal.go ReduceOpts.Tol, staircase.go ctrbfFloor.

[w14 #5 tf/review] Owner decision, Reduce default Tol (review item 6): MATLAB minreal documents tol = sqrt(eps). Measured with that default: TestReduceIssue26PIPlantLoop drops to order 1; KALMAN_SWEEP_DIAG=3 gives 174 under-counts and 277 response errors (base 9); with Equalize forced there are still O(1) response errors at the correct order (e.g. rr=4.71 on id 1185 and 12.5 on id 1609, seed PCG(id, 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15), kB=8). ## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-20, reconciled with MathWorks doc)
The MathWorks minreal page does not mention balancing, scaling, prescaling or ssbal. Its Algorithms section says only "Transfer functions are first converted to zero-pole-gain form", and the default tol is sqrt(eps), a pole-zero matching tolerance in a different algorithm. Parity is silent on Equalize.
- Tol: keep the ctrbf floor. ReduceOpts.Tol stays as the user override. Document why sqrt(eps) is not copied: it is a different quantity, and the measured sqrt(eps) default gave 174 under-counts and 277 response errors at d=3, and dropped TestReduceIssue26PIPlantLoop to order 1.
- Equalize: decide by data. Evaluate Equalize-on TOGETHER with one shared ctrbf floor across Reduce, CtrbF and ObsvF on the d=0..4 Kalman sweep.
  - Flip the default iff the combination is no worse than the current default at every d: no new over-counts (each one is a stable→unstable flip) and no new response errors.
  - If you flip it, add NoEqualize (zero value = prescale) instead of silently inverting the Equalize bool at minimal.go:37.
  - Otherwise keep the default off and document the 92-case d=4 trade-off.
  - Either outcome closes this task.

Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Cross-ref FRD wrong-sign task (stable plants, real instability) — this one is stable designs, sign policy only.

[w14 #14 pidtune/SIVH4J] TunePID PD returns gains of opposite sign on integrating plants. Repro: TransferFunc num {8.2}, den {1,-1}, Dt 0.05, then StateSpace and TunePID(ctx, sys, PidtunePD, PIDTuningOptions{}). It returns Kp 0.0344, Kd -0.0019; with PhaseMargin 30 it returns Kp 0.0273, Kd -0.0036. Pidtune PD on the same plant gives same-sign gains (Kp 0.0378, Kd +3.1e-4, Tf 8.2e-4), and MATLAB pidtune never gives mixed signs. IP3XIC k=10 PD does the same (fix: Kp 0.79, Kd -1.23e5). The designs are stable with |S| <= 4, so this is about the sign policy, not robustness. Cause: pidTuningDCSign returns 0 once Pidtune recognises an integrator, so pidTuningSignConsistent accepts any mix of signs (pid_tuning.go, pidTuningDCSign and pidTuningSignConsistent; TunePID default PD path). Owner call: whether integrating plants should require same-sign gains, perhaps using the sign of the integrator's residue. Note SIVH4J's new test pins two such mixed-sign PD designs as acceptable for |S|.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-20): require same-sign gains; the sign comes from the integrator residue
MATLAB pidtune never returns mixed signs, and Pidtune already gives same-sign gains on the same plant.
- When integratingDCGain (internal dcGain(false)) is ±Inf, pidTuningDCSign returns sign(integratingDCGain) instead of 0.
- Do not touch the unstable-plant sign rule (YVAIMU / pidtuneGainSign); reuse it.
- Allowed flips: mixed-sign → same-sign design, or mixed-sign → unattainable. BLOCKING: a same-sign base design that changes and then fails the oracle.
- Re-pin the two mixed-sign PD designs in the SIVH4J test.
Priority CORE. Put it in the wave 15 pidtune track together with GMED3W and EPFTFX.

[w14 #25 riccati/review] Dare returns a silently wrong X for benign plants once n >= 65 (2n > 128); likely a gonum blocked-QZ or ordering threshold. Repro with bench_test.go generators: A=benchDiscreteA(n), B=benchB(n,5), Q=benchSymPD(n), R=I5, then Dare(A,B,Q,R,nil). Relative Riccati residual (dareRelResidual) at base 0c02feb and 4a25ae4: about 7e-14 at n=60..64, then 0.32 (n=65), 0.24 (66), 0.15 (67), 0.078 (68), 0.48 (70), 0.022 (100), 0.015 (120). X error against Hewer is 1.54 at n=70 and 0.53 at n=100. NoScaling gives identical numbers, so scaling is not the cause. Care with E=I at the same sizes is accurate (rel err 1e-12), so the problem is specific to the discrete pencil. Dare with E=I shows the same wrong residual and is NOT repaired by this branch, because refineDare skips E != nil. Without E, the new Hewer refinement now masks it (n=100 residual 3e-15), but BenchmarkDare_N100_M5 was timing a wrong answer. Files: riccati.go generalizedStableSubspace (Dgges with SortSelected), gonum lapack Dgges/Dhgeqz/Dtgsen/Dgghd3. Next step: compare the pencil eigenvalues to eig(A-BK) from Hewer's K at n=70 to tell a Dhgeqz fault from a Dtgsen/vectors fault. Once fixed, re-check that benign n=150-200 residuals stay below the 1e-12 refine trigger.

[w14 #24 riccati/BFT5QM] gonum (file in gonum repo): Dgges/Dhgeqz fails to converge (ErrSchurFailed) at isolated cost scales on a well-posed symplectic extended pencil; the cost scales on either side solve. Repro: data of TestDare_LaterPassFailureRetried "qz" in riccati_rescue_test.go (A 3x3, rho about 200, Q about 1.5e5, R=1.43e6). After problem.scale (state scale t=[4,4,4]), call generalizedStableSubspace(false, problem.pencil()) with balanced=true at sigma=2^k. Every k=-10..80 in steps of 5 (plus the 2^54 production solve) gives: 2^54, 2^55, 2^65 and 2^75 fail on arm64 and amd64, while 2^50 and 2^60 solve with residual 1e-12. Under NoScaling, 2^55 and 2^70 fail while 2^65 solves. In a second plant (TestDare_LaterPassFailureRetried "indefinite", A 4x4), 2^45, 2^75 and 2^80 fail. controlsys now works around this with retryCost (riccati.go), but the QZ non-convergence itself is upstream.
